title: CLAUDE.md
text: build_contrast_analysis() recommended entry point. method dispatches Facade class wires strategy → model → contrasts → moderation internally. authoritative facade list .seed_facade_registry() table R/ContrastsFacades.R; query runtime lookup_facade(name). Facades split input/output hierarchy shape — lookup_facade(name)$needs returns one two values: needs = "" — facade emits contrasts hierarchy level input (protein → protein FC, peptide/precursor → peptide/precursor FC; subject_Id == hierarchy_keys). Lives R/ContrastsFacades.R: lm, rlm, lm_missing, lm_impute, limma, limma_impute, limma_voom, limma_voom_impute, deqms, deqms_voom, firth, limpa needs = "nested" — facade takes child-level input (peptide/precursor) emits parent-level (protein) contrasts; subject_Id strict subset hierarchy_keys. Lives R/ContrastsChildToParentFacades.R: lmer_nested, ropeca_nested, firth_nested, limpa_nested -level lmer/ropeca facades — mixed-model ROPECA analyses nested-.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: config$nr_children names column tracking child-feature counts (e.g. peptides per protein). get_Aggregator() rollup, protein×sample row gets count — nr_children sample-wise. peptide/precursor-level data typically 1. Two distinct uses: Fitting weights (sample-wise): Aggregated facades (lm, limma, lm_missing, lm_impute, deqms) pass nr_children weights default lm() limma::lmFit(). -weights protein intensities derived fewer peptides given sample. Disable weights = NULL. DEqMS variance moderation (experiment-wide): ContrastsDEqMSFacade additionally aggregates nr_children via max() per protein across samples count-dependent variance shrinkage. separate fitting weights. Protein-level input must carry nr_children. column missing, setup_analysis() adds set 1 warning — defeats purpose aggregated data actual peptide count matters.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Decorator/Composition: LFQData factory methods (get_Transformer(), get_Plotter(), etc.) return decorator objects wrap LFQData. Decorators hold reference lfq field. Method chaining: Transformer methods return self chaining, access result via $lfq: Strategy pattern models: Strategy R6 classes models: StrategyLM, StrategyRLM, StrategyLmer, StrategyLogistf — model_fun, isSingular, contrast_fun, df_residual, sigma methods. Wrapper functions strategy_lm(), strategy_rlm(), strategy_lmer(), strategy_logistf() create instances. strategy_limma() returns plain list (formula, trend, robust, weights) consumed build_model_limma(). Config immutability: AnalysisConfiguration always deep-cloned passed new LFQData instances. Never modify config -place existing LFQData.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Flat R6 class maps column roles data: - hierarchy: ordered measurement levels (protein_Id → peptide_Id → precursor_Id → fragment_Id). hierarchy_depth controls level modelled. - factors: explanatory variables (group, treatment). factor_depth controls interaction depth. - work_intensity: response column. Uses stack (set_response() / pop_response() / get_response()) working multiple intensity columns. - file_name: sample identifier column. Concrete config factories (e.g. create_config_Skyline(), create_config_Spectronaut_Peptide()) tidyMS_R6_ConcreteConfigurations.R (now removed — create_config_MQ_peptide() dead code). Remaining factories downstream packages.

title: Contrast Facades with Two-Factor Subgroup Design
text: vignette demonstrates build_contrast_analysis() facade workflow dataset two factors (e.g. treatment genotype), yielding four subgroups: C_WT, T_WT, C_KO, T_KO. define contrasts: T_C_gv_WT = T_WT - C_WT T_C_gv_KO = T_KO - C_KO WT_KO_comp = T_C_gv_WT - T_C_gv_KO start simulated two-factor peptide data, derive single subgroup factor, run protein-input peptide-input facades contrast specification. See ContrastFacades.Rmd one-factor introduction.

what: Simulate two-factor data and encode subgroups
title: Contrast Facades with Two-Factor Subgroup Design
code: options(prolfqua.vectorize = TRUE)  dd <- sim_lfq_data_2factor_config(   Nprot = 80,   with_missing = TRUE,   weight_missing = 1,   PEPTIDE = TRUE,   seed = 7 )  cfg_subgroup <- dd$config$clone(deep = TRUE) data_subgroup <- dd$data |>   dplyr::mutate(     Condition = dplyr::recode(Treatment, A = "C", B = "T"),     Genotype = dplyr::recode(Background, Z = "WT", X = "KO"),     Subgroup = paste(Condition, Genotype, sep = "_")   )  cfg_subgroup$factors <- c(Subgroup = "Subgroup") cfg_subgroup$factor_depth <- 1  lfq_peptide_2f <- LFQData$new(data_subgroup, cfg_subgroup) lfq_peptide_2f <- lfq_peptide_2f$get_Transformer()$log2()$lfq  lfq_protein_2f <- lfq_peptide_2f$get_Aggregator()$aggregate()  lfq_peptide_2f$hierarchy_keys() ## [1] "protein_Id" "peptide_Id" lfq_protein_2f$hierarchy_keys() ## [1] "protein_Id" lfq_protein_2f$nr_children_col() ## [1] "nr_children_protein_Id"

title: Contrast Facades with Two-Factor Subgroup Design
text: following facades require aggregated input. firth included can fitted directly aggregated protein input. protein-input facades share interface report protein-level contrasts, outputs can combined directly. facades combine several underlying result types, lm_missing, modelName column still tells individual rows came .
code: fa_lm_2f <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein_2f,   "~ Subgroup",   contrasts_2f,   method = "lm" )  fa_limma_2f <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein_2f,   "~ Subgroup",   contrasts_2f,   method = "limma" )  fa_limma_impute_2f <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein_2f,   "~ Subgroup",   contrasts_2f,   method = "limma_impute" )  fa_lm_missing_2f <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein_2f,   "~ Subgroup",   contrasts_2f,   method = "lm_missing" )  fa_deqms_2f <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein_2f,   "~ Subgroup",   contrasts_2f,   method = "deqms" )  fa_lm_impute_2f <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein_2f,   "~ Subgroup",   contrasts_2f,   method = "lm_impute" )  fa_firth_protein_2f <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein_2f,   "~ Subgroup",   contrasts_2f,   method = "firth" ) # Proteins missing in the baseline lm facade (used to flag rescued proteins) lm_missing_ids_2f <- fa_lm_2f$get_missing() |>   dplyr::select(protein_Id, contrast) |>   dplyr::mutate(rescued = TRUE)  results_protein_2f <- bind_rows(   fa_lm_2f$get_contrasts(),   fa_limma_2f$get_contrasts(),   fa_limma_impute_2f$get_contrasts(),   fa_lm_missing_2f$get_contrasts(),   fa_lm_impute_2f$get_contrasts(),   fa_deqms_2f$get_contrasts(),   fa_firth_protein_2f$get_contrasts() ) |>   dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c(     "facade", "modelName", "protein_Id", "contrast", "avgAbd", "diff", "FDR",     "statistic", "std.error", "df", "p.value", "conf.low", "conf.high",     "sigma"   ))) |>   dplyr::left_join(lm_missing_ids_2f, by = c("protein_Id", "contrast")) |>   dplyr::mutate(     rescued = dplyr::coalesce(rescued, FALSE),     significant = FDR < 0.1 & abs(diff) > 0.5   )  results_protein_2f |>   dplyr::count(facade, name = "n_results") ## # A tibble: 7 × 2 ##   facade       n_results ##   <chr>            <int> ## 1 deqms              232 ## 2 firth              232 ## 3 limma              232 ## 4 limma_impute       240 ## 5 lm                 232 ## 6 lm_impute          240 ## 7 lm_missing         240 results_protein_2f |>   dplyr::count(facade, contrast, modelName, name = "n_results") ## # A tibble: 30 × 4 ##    facade       contrast   modelName      n_results ##    <chr>        <chr>      <chr>              <int> ##  1 deqms        T_C_gv_KO  WaldTest_DEqMS        79 ##  2 deqms        T_C_gv_WT  WaldTest_DEqMS        77 ##  3 deqms        WT_KO_comp WaldTest_DEqMS        76 ##  4 firth        T_C_gv_KO  WaldTestFirth         79 ##  5 firth        T_C_gv_WT  WaldTestFirth         77 ##  6 firth        WT_KO_comp WaldTestFirth         76 ##  7 limma        T_C_gv_KO  limma                 79 ##  8 limma        T_C_gv_WT  limma                 77 ##  9 limma        WT_KO_comp limma                 76 ## 10 limma_impute T_C_gv_KO  limma                 76 ## # ℹ 20 more rows

code: fa_lmer_2f <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_peptide_2f,   "~ Subgroup + (1 | peptide_Id) + (1 | sampleName)",   contrasts_2f,   method = "lmer_nested" )  fa_ropeca_2f <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_peptide_2f,   "~ Subgroup",   contrasts_2f,   method = "ropeca_nested" )  fa_firth_peptide_2f <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_peptide_2f,   "~ Subgroup",   contrasts_2f,   method = "firth_nested" ) results_peptide_2f <- bind_rows(   fa_lmer_2f$get_contrasts(),   fa_ropeca_2f$get_contrasts(),   fa_firth_peptide_2f$get_contrasts() ) |>   dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c(     "facade", "modelName", "protein_Id", "contrast", "avgAbd", "diff", "FDR",     "statistic", "std.error", "df", "p.value", "conf.low", "conf.high",     "sigma"   ))) |>   dplyr::mutate(     significant = FDR < 0.1 & abs(diff) > 0.5   )  results_peptide_2f |>   dplyr::count(facade, name = "n_results") ## # A tibble: 3 × 2 ##   facade        n_results ##   <chr>             <int> ## 1 firth_nested        240 ## 2 lmer_nested         179 ## 3 ropeca_nested       231 ggplot(results_peptide_2f, aes(x = diff, y = -log10(p.value), color = significant)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2) +   facet_grid(contrast ~ facade, scales = "free_y") +   geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.5, 0.5), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +   geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.1), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +   scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "firebrick", `FALSE` = "grey70")) +   labs(     x = "log2 fold change",     y = "-log10(p.value)",     color = "FDR < 0.1\nand |diff| > 0.5"   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

title: Contrast Facades with Parallel Designs
text: build_contrast_analysis() provides common front-end several contrast backends: lm limma limma_impute limpa (requires AggregateLimpa DPC-based aggregation standard errors) lmer ropeca lm_missing lm_impute deqms firth expose basic interface: get_contrasts(), get_Plotter(), to_wide(). examples return protein-level contrasts. important difference required input level: lm, limma, limma_impute, lm_missing, lm_impute, deqms require aggregated protein-level data limpa requires protein-level data AggregateLimpa (provides standard errors observation counts vooma precision weighting) lmer ropeca require lower-level measurements peptides nested within proteins, still report protein-level contrasts firth can used either aggregated protein-level data nested peptide-level data still reports protein-level contrasts vignette starts one simulated peptide-level experiment, aggregates protein level, demonstrates families facades separately.

title: Contrast Facades with Parallel Designs
text: aggregation step produces protein-level intensities keeping count metadata LFQData object. DEqMS facade uses lfq_protein$nr_children_col() directly, extra count table passed around.
code: options(prolfqua.vectorize = TRUE)  istar <- sim_lfq_data_peptide_config(Nprot = 80, seed = 42)   lfq_peptide <- LFQData$new(istar$data, istar$config) lfq_peptide <- lfq_peptide$get_Transformer()$log2()$lfq  lfq_protein <- lfq_peptide$get_Aggregator()$aggregate()  lfq_peptide$hierarchy_keys() ## [1] "protein_Id" "peptide_Id" lfq_protein$hierarchy_keys() ## [1] "protein_Id" lfq_protein$nr_children_col() ## [1] "nr_children_protein_Id"

code: fa_lm <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein,   "~ group_",   contrasts,   method = "lm" )  fa_limma <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein,   "~ group_",   contrasts,   method = "limma" )  fa_limma_impute <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein,   "~ group_",   contrasts,   method = "limma_impute" )  fa_lm_missing <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein,   "~ group_",   contrasts,   method = "lm_missing" )  fa_deqms <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein,   "~ group_",   contrasts,   method = "deqms" )  fa_lm_impute <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein,   "~ group_",   contrasts,   method = "lm_impute" )  fa_firth_protein <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_protein,   "~ group_",   contrasts,   method = "firth" )

title: Contrast Facades with Parallel Designs
text: limpa facade different protein-level facades: requires aggregation step via AggregateLimpa, uses limpa’s Detection Probability Curve (DPC) aggregate peptides proteins producing per-protein, per-sample standard errors. SEs feed bivariate vooma variance model precision weighting. protein-input facades share interface report protein-level contrasts, outputs can combined directly. facades combine several underlying result types, lm_missing, modelName column still tells individual rows came .
code: lfq_limpa <- AggregateLimpa$new(lfq_peptide, "protein")$aggregate()  fa_limpa <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_limpa,   "~ group_",   contrasts,   method = "limpa" ) # Proteins missing in the baseline lm facade (used to flag rescued proteins) lm_missing_ids <- fa_lm$get_missing() |>   dplyr::select(protein_Id, contrast) |>   dplyr::mutate(rescued = TRUE)  results_limpa <- if (requireNamespace("limpa", quietly = TRUE)) {   fa_limpa$get_contrasts() } else {   data.frame() }  results_protein <- bind_rows(   fa_lm$get_contrasts(),   fa_limma$get_contrasts(),   fa_limma_impute$get_contrasts(),   fa_lm_missing$get_contrasts(),   fa_lm_impute$get_contrasts(),   fa_deqms$get_contrasts(),   fa_firth_protein$get_contrasts(),   results_limpa ) |>   dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c(     "facade", "modelName", "protein_Id", "contrast", "avgAbd", "diff", "FDR",     "statistic", "std.error", "df", "p.value", "conf.low", "conf.high",     "sigma"   ))) |>   dplyr::left_join(lm_missing_ids, by = c("protein_Id", "contrast")) |>   dplyr::mutate(     rescued = dplyr::coalesce(rescued, FALSE),     significant = FDR < 0.1 & abs(diff) > 0.5   )  results_protein |>   dplyr::count(facade, name = "n_results") ## # A tibble: 8 × 2 ##   facade       n_results ##   <chr>            <int> ## 1 deqms              157 ## 2 firth              157 ## 3 limma              155 ## 4 limma_impute       160 ## 5 limpa              160 ## 6 lm                 157 ## 7 lm_impute          160 ## 8 lm_missing         160 results_protein |>   dplyr::count(facade, contrast, modelName, name = "n_results") ## # A tibble: 22 × 4 ##    facade       contrast  modelName      n_results ##    <chr>        <chr>     <chr>              <int> ##  1 deqms        A_vs_Ctrl WaldTest_DEqMS        78 ##  2 deqms        B_vs_Ctrl WaldTest_DEqMS        79 ##  3 firth        A_vs_Ctrl WaldTestFirth         78 ##  4 firth        B_vs_Ctrl WaldTestFirth         79 ##  5 limma        A_vs_Ctrl limma                 78 ##  6 limma        B_vs_Ctrl limma                 77 ##  7 limma_impute A_vs_Ctrl limma                 77 ##  8 limma_impute A_vs_Ctrl limma_imputed          3 ##  9 limma_impute B_vs_Ctrl limma                 77 ## 10 limma_impute B_vs_Ctrl limma_imputed          3 ## # ℹ 12 more rows

title: Contrast Facades with Parallel Designs
text: peptide-input facades take peptide/precursor-level LFQData return protein-level contrasts. defined R/ContrastsChildToParentFacades.R use *_nested method keys: lmer_nested, ropeca_nested, firth_nested, limpa_nested. firth_nested peptide-input counterpart protein-input firth shown . ropeca_nested aggregates peptide evidence back proteins, whereas lmer_nested models nested peptide structure directly reporting protein-level contrasts. firth_nested also reports protein-level contrasts: proteins exactly one peptide fitted without added peptide term, proteins multiple peptides fitted lowest hierarchy key added internally. Volcano plots peptide-level facades. Rows contrasts, columns backends.
code: fa_lmer <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_peptide,   "~ group_ + (1 | peptide_Id) + (1 | sampleName)",   contrasts,   method = "lmer_nested" )  fa_ropeca <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_peptide,   "~ group_",   contrasts,   method = "ropeca_nested" )  fa_firth_peptide <- build_contrast_analysis(   lfq_peptide,   "~ group_",   contrasts,   method = "firth_nested" ) results_peptide <- bind_rows(   fa_lmer$get_contrasts(),   fa_ropeca$get_contrasts(),   fa_firth_peptide$get_contrasts() ) |>   dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c(     "facade", "modelName", "protein_Id", "contrast", "avgAbd", "diff", "FDR",     "statistic", "std.error", "df", "p.value", "conf.low", "conf.high",     "sigma"   ))) |>   dplyr::mutate(     significant = FDR < 0.1 & abs(diff) > 0.5   )  results_peptide |>   dplyr::count(facade, name = "n_results") ## # A tibble: 3 × 2 ##   facade        n_results ##   <chr>             <int> ## 1 firth_nested        160 ## 2 lmer_nested         102 ## 3 ropeca_nested       157 ggplot(results_peptide, aes(x = diff, y = -log10(p.value), color = significant)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2) +   facet_grid(contrast ~ facade, scales = "free_y") +   geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.5, 0.5), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +   geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.1), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +   scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "firebrick", `FALSE` = "grey70")) +   labs(     x = "log2 fold change",     y = "-log10(p.value)",     color = "FDR < 0.1\nand |diff| > 0.5"   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

title: DEqMS-style Count-Dependent Variance Moderation
text: vignette demonstrates ContrastsModeratedDEqMS, count-dependent variance shrinkage method inspired DEqMS approach (Zhu et al., 2020). drop-alternative ContrastsModerated: ContrastsModerated (standard): applies single global prior variance proteins — every protein shrunk toward value. ContrastsModeratedDEqMS (count-dependent): prior variance depends number peptides/PSMs used quantify protein. Proteins quantified many peptides get less shrinkage (variance already well estimated); proteins peptides get . matters proteomics quantification depth varies hugely across proteins. protein quantified 20 peptides much better-estimated variance one 2 peptides, receive prior. user-facing API identical ContrastsModerated: downstream methods (get_contrasts, get_Plotter, to_wide, merge_contrasts_results).

title: DEqMS-style Count-Dependent Variance Moderation
text: Fit LOESS: log(sigma^2) ~ log2(peptide_count) — captures count-dependent variance trend. Estimate prior df (d0): residual variance around LOESS curve, using trigammaInverse approach (math limma/squeezeVarRob). Count-specific prior variance: s0^2(count) varies per protein, derived fitted LOESS curve. Posterior variance: Bayesian shrinkage combining observed prior: var.post = (d0 * s0^2(count) + df * sigma^2) / (d0 + df) Moderated t-statistics p-values recomputed posterior variance.

title: DEqMS-style Count-Dependent Variance Moderation
text: core diagnostic plot DEqMS approach. expect log(sigma^2) decrease increasing peptide count, LOESS curve captures trend. Residual variance decreases peptide count. LOESS curve (blue) defines count-specific prior variance.
code: # Get the unmoderated results with sigma and count contr_raw <- contr_lm$get_contrasts() contr_raw <- inner_join(   contr_raw,   count_per_prot,   by = "protein_Id" )  # Plot for one contrast one_contrast <- contr_raw |> filter(contrast == levels(factor(contrast))[1])  ggplot(one_contrast, aes(x = log2(nr_peptides), y = log(sigma^2))) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 2) +   geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.75, color = "steelblue", se = TRUE) +   labs(x = "log2(peptide count)",        y = "log(residual variance)",        title = paste("Variance vs. peptide count —", one_contrast$contrast[1])) +   theme_minimal()

title: Limma Backend for prolfqua
text: vignette demonstrates limma backend prolfqua’s modelling pipeline. limma backend drop-alternative per-protein lm + squeezeVar pipeline. approaches fit linear models perform empirical Bayes variance shrinkage, : prolfqua default (strategy_lm + Contrasts + ContrastsModerated): fits one lm() per protein, applies prolfqua’s squeezeVarRob moderation. limma backend (strategy_limma + ContrastsLimma): uses limma’s matrix-based lmFit + contrasts.fit + eBayes pipeline directly. user-facing API identical: formula specification, contrast specification, downstream methods (get_contrasts, get_Plotter, to_wide, merge_contrasts_results).

title: Limma Backend for prolfqua
text: use simulated protein-level data 3 groups (, B, Ctrl) missing values.

title: Limma Backend for prolfqua
text: strategy_limma function accepts trend robust arguments passed limma::eBayes: trend = TRUE: allows prior variance depend average intensity (useful variance intensity-dependent) robust = TRUE: uses robust empirical Bayes procedure (resistant outlier variances)

title: Limma Backend for prolfqua
text: vooma (variance modelling observational level) backend extends limma observation-level precision weights derived mean-variance trend. analogous voom RNA-seq applied proteomics intensities. key idea: instead assuming equal variance across observations, vooma estimates smooth mean-variance relationship -weights observations higher expected variance. API mirrors standard limma pipeline — difference calling build_model_limma_voom instead build_model_limma.  plot shows sqrt(sigma) vs average log-expression. red curve lowess trend used derive per-observation weights.
code: strat_voom <- strategy_limma("transformedIntensity ~ group_") mod_voom <- build_model_limma_voom(transformed, strat_voom, plot = TRUE) contr_voom <- ContrastsLimma$new(mod_voom, contr_spec) res_voom <- contr_voom$get_contrasts()

title: Limma Backend for prolfqua
text: limpa backend uses limpa’s Detection Probability Curve (DPC) probabilistic missing value handling, followed vooma precision weighting incorporates quantification standard errors. three-step pipeline : AggregateLimpa — estimates DPC, quantifies features using limpa::dpcQuant() (peptide→protein) limpa::dpcQuantByRow() (-level imputation). Produces standard errors observation counts. build_model_limpa — fits vooma model using limpa::voomaLmFitWithImputation() SEs bivariate predictor ContrastsLimma — reused -since output standard MArrayLM show two examples: aggregation protein level staying peptide level.

title: Limma Backend for prolfqua
text: AggregateLimpa wraps limpa::dpc() (DPC estimation) limpa::dpcQuant() (protein quantification). output protein-level LFQData three value columns: intensity, standard error (config$opt_se), observation count (config$nr_children). Missing values probabilistically integrated quantification — fabricated numbers imputed.
code: agg <- AggregateLimpa$new(lfq_peptide, "protein") lfq_protein_limpa <- agg$aggregate()  data.frame(   Property = c("Input hierarchy", "Output hierarchy", "Response column",                "SE column", "Nr children column", "NAs in output",                "DPC beta0", "DPC beta1"),   Value = c(     paste(lfq_peptide$hierarchy_keys(), collapse = " > "),     paste(lfq_protein_limpa$hierarchy_keys(), collapse = " > "),     lfq_protein_limpa$response(),     lfq_protein_limpa$get_config()$opt_se,     lfq_protein_limpa$nr_children_col(),     sum(is.na(lfq_protein_limpa$data_long()[[lfq_protein_limpa$response()]])),     round(agg$dpc_result$dpc[1], 3),     round(agg$dpc_result$dpc[2], 3)   ) ) |> knitr::kable()

what: Fit the DE model with dpcDE()
title: Using limpa Directly on prolfqua Simulated Data
text: dpcDE() thin wrapper (9 lines code) calls voomaLmFitWithImputation(). passes : vooma SEs already estimated? SEs dpcQuantByRow()/dpcQuant() per-observation quantification uncertainties. limma needs observation-level precision weights linear model. voomaLmFitWithImputation() converts SEs proper weights via bivariate lowess trend: Fit initial lmFit() get per-protein residual SDs (sigma) Model sqrt(sigma) ~ average_intensity + log(SE) using bivariate linear predictor Smooth lowess get mean-variance trend function f() Compute weights w = 1/f(fitted_value)^4 — inverse fourth power predicted SD analogous voom converts RNA-seq counts weights via mean-variance trend, extended second predictor (SE quantification). two predictors capture different variance sources: Average intensity: classical mean-variance relationship proteomics log(SE): additional variance quantification uncertainty (missing precursors = larger SE = lower weight) Additionally, voomaLmFitWithImputation() corrects residual degrees freedom proteins entire groups missing (values imputed), preventing overconfident inference.  plot shows sqrt(sigma) vs combined predictor (average intensity + log SE). red line lowess trend used derive precision weights.
code: # From limpa/R/dpcDE.R: dpcDE <- function(y, design, plot=TRUE, ...) {   eps <- 1e-6   voomaLmFitWithImputation(     y         = y,                              # EList with $E and $other     imputed   = !y$other$n.observations,        # logical matrix: TRUE where value was missing     design    = design,                         # design matrix     predictor = log(y$other$standard.error+eps),# log(SE) as precision predictor     plot      = plot,     ...   ) } fit_pep <- limpa::dpcDE(y_peptide, design, plot = TRUE) fit_pep <- limma::eBayes(fit_pep)

what: Step 4b: DF correction for fully imputed groups
title: Using limpa Directly on prolfqua Simulated Data
text: peptide values imputed within design-matrix group, fitted value group determined entirely imputed data — residual df reduced. uses hat matrix detect cases.
code: h <- 1 - hat(design)  # leverage complement per sample df_imputed <- imputed_matrix %*% (1 - h)  # effective imputed df per peptide  n_affected <- sum(df_imputed > 0.9999) cat("Peptides with fully-imputed groups:", n_affected, "\n") ## Peptides with fully-imputed groups: 16 # For affected peptides, refit on observed-only data to get corrected sigma/df if (n_affected > 0) {   affected_idx <- which(rowSums(df_imputed > 0.9999) > 0)   E_affected <- y_pep$E[affected_idx, , drop = FALSE]   E_affected_NA <- E_affected   E_affected_NA[imputed_matrix[affected_idx, , drop = FALSE]] <- NA   fit_NA <- suppressWarnings(limma::lmFit(E_affected_NA, design))    cat("Corrected df.residual for affected peptides:", fit_NA$df.residual[1:min(5, length(fit_NA$df.residual))], "\n")    # Replace sigma and df for affected rows   fit0$sigma[affected_idx] <- fit_NA$sigma   fit0$df.residual[affected_idx] <- fit_NA$df.residual } ## Corrected df.residual for affected peptides: 7 7 6 7 6

what: Step 4c: Bivariate linear predictor (average intensity + log SE)
title: Using limpa Directly on prolfqua Simulated Data
text: key innovation standard vooma. Instead modelling variance function average intensity alone, limpa uses TWO predictors: sx = average log2 expression per peptide (classical mean-variance axis) sxc = average log(SE) per peptide (quantification uncertainty axis) linear model sqrt(sigma) ~ sx + sxc combines single predictor.
code:
# Average expression per peptide sx <- rowMeans(y_pep$E, na.rm = TRUE)  # Residual SD (square root for the variance trend) sy <- sqrt(fit0$sigma)  # Average log(SE) per peptide — the precision predictor sxc <- rowMeans(predictor, na.rm = TRUE)  # Bivariate linear model: sqrt(sigma) ~ 1 + avg_intensity + avg_log_SE vartrend <- lm.fit(cbind(1, sx, sxc), sy) beta <- coef(vartrend) cat("Variance trend coefficients:
") ## Variance trend coefficients: cat("  Intercept:", round(beta[1], 4), "
") ##   Intercept: 0.6832 cat("  avg_intensity:", round(beta[2], 4), "
") ##   avg_intensity: -0.0789 cat("  avg_log_SE:", round(beta[3], 4),     ifelse(beta[3] > 0, " (higher SE → higher variance, as expected)", ""), "
") ##   avg_log_SE: 0.0119  (higher SE → higher variance, as expected) # Combined predictor (per-peptide summary for the lowess x-axis) sx_combined <- vartrend$fitted.values  # Per-observation combined predictor (for computing weights later) mu_combined <- beta[1] + beta[2] * fitted_values + beta[3] * predictor

code: span <- limma::chooseLowessSpan(nrow(y_pep), small.n = 50, min.span = 0.3, power = 1/3) cat("Lowess span:", round(span, 3), "\n") ## Lowess span: 0.783 l <- lowess(sx_combined, sy, f = span)  # Plot the trend plot(sx_combined, sy,      xlab = "Combined predictor (avg intensity + log SE)",      ylab = "Sqrt(sigma)",      pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = "grey40",      main = "vooma variance trend (manual)") lines(l, col = "red", lwd = 2)

text: lowess trend gives function f() predicts sqrt(sigma) combined predictor. Weights inverse fourth power: w = 1/f(mu)^4. means observations higher predicted variance get lower weight. Imputed values get systematically lower weights larger SEs, pushes high-variance end trend.
code:
# Interpolating function from the lowess fit f_trend <- approxfun(l, rule = 2, ties = list("ordered", mean))  # Per-observation weights: 1/f(mu_ij)^4 w_manual <- 1 / f_trend(mu_combined)^4 dim(w_manual) <- dim(y_pep$E)  cat("Weights matrix:", dim(w_manual), "
") ## Weights matrix: 152 15 cat("Weight range:", round(range(w_manual), 2), "
") ## Weight range: 124.89 606.68 cat("Weight median:", round(median(w_manual), 2), "
") ## Weight median: 165.13 # Show how weights relate to missingness cat("
Mean weight for observed values:", round(mean(w_manual[!imputed_matrix]), 2), "
") ##  ## Mean weight for observed values: 237.64 cat("Mean weight for imputed values:", round(mean(w_manual[imputed_matrix]), 2), "
") ## Mean weight for imputed values: 150.99

text: dpcQuantByRow() quantifies peptide independently, returning EList $E (complete, NAs), $$standard.error (quantification uncertainty), $$n.observations (observation counts). dpcQuant() additionally aggregates peptides proteins, fitting Bayesian additive model per protein. EList gains $genes$NPrec (peptide counts) hyperparameter fields ($dpc, $prior.mean, $prior.sd, $prior.logFC). dpcDE() thin wrapper calls voomaLmFitWithImputation() : imputed = !y$$n.observations — flags values missing predictor = log(y$$standard.error) — SEs variance predictor vooma top SEs? SEs dpcQuant() per-observation quantification uncertainties. voomaLmFitWithImputation() uses second predictor bivariate variance trend (sqrt(sigma) ~ avg_intensity + log(SE)) derive observation-level precision weights w = 1/f(fitted)^4. captures classical mean-variance relationship additional heteroscedasticity missing values. also corrects residual DF proteins entire groups imputed.

text: Combines vooma precision weights (mean-variance trend) DEqMS count-dependent variance moderation. Vooma runs without external weights captures mean-variance relationship; peptide count enters solely DEqMS moderation, avoiding double-counting. Pipeline: strategy_limma (weights = NULL) -> build_model_limma_voom -> ContrastsLimma (eBayes = FALSE) -> ContrastsModeratedDEqMS.

title: Create an imputed lm wrapper — new_lm_imputed
Create an imputed lm wrapper — new_lm_imputed
code: # Fit a normal lm, then wrap it with borrowed covariance dat <- data.frame(group_ = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 4),                   y = c(20.1, 20.5, 19.8, 20.3, 22.1, 22.4, 21.9, 22.2)) fit <- lm(y ~ group_, data = dat)  # Wrap with borrowed variance (in practice these come from donor pool) wrapped <- prolfqua:::new_lm_imputed(fit,   borrowed_vcov = vcov(fit),   borrowed_sigma = 0.8,   borrowed_df = 6,   n_observed = 5)  # S3 dispatch returns borrowed values stopifnot(inherits(wrapped, "lm_imputed")) stopifnot(sigma(wrapped) == 0.8) stopifnot(df.residual(wrapped) == 6) # coefficients() still dispatches to underlying lm stopifnot(identical(coefficients(wrapped), coefficients(fit)))

code: skylineconfig <- AnalysisConfiguration$new() skylineconfig$file_name <- "Replicate.Name" skylineconfig$hierarchy[["protein_Id"]] <- "Protein.Name" skylineconfig$hierarchy[["peptide_Id"]] <- "Peptide.Sequence" skylineconfig$hierarchy[["precursor_Id"]] <- c("Peptide.Sequence", "Precursor.Charge") skylineconfig$hierarchy[["fragment_Id"]] <- c(   "Peptide.Sequence", "Precursor.Charge",   "Fragment.Ion", "Product.Charge" ) skylineconfig$ident_q_value <- "Detection.Q.Value" skylineconfig$set_response("Area") skylineconfig$isotope_label <- "Isotope.Label.Type" skylineconfig$factors[["Time"]] = "Sampling.Time.Point" sample_analysis <- setup_analysis(prolfqua_data('data_skylinePRMSample_A')$data, skylineconfig) #> creating sampleName from file_name column #> Warning: no nr_children column specified in the data, adding column nr_children and setting to 1. #> completing cases #> completing cases done #> setup done  # Example with normValue column (e.g., creatinine) set.seed(1234) data <- sim_lfq_data(Nprot = 10, PEPTIDE = TRUE, N = 4) data$nr_children <- 1 data$isotopeLabel <- "light" data$qValue <- 0  # Add creatinine values per sample (not per protein/peptide) sample_creatinine <- data |> dplyr::select(sample) |> dplyr::distinct() |>   dplyr::mutate(creatinine = rnorm(dplyr::n(), mean = 100, sd = 10)) data <- dplyr::inner_join(data, sample_creatinine, by = "sample")  config <- AnalysisConfiguration$new() config$file_name = "sample" config$factors["group_"] = "group" config$hierarchy[["protein_Id"]] = c("proteinID", "idtype2") config$hierarchy[["peptide_Id"]] = "peptideID" config$set_response("abundance") config$norm_value = "creatinine"  adata <- setup_analysis(data, config) #> creating sampleName from file_name column #> completing cases #> completing cases done #> setup done

code: bb <- prolfqua::sim_lfq_data_protein_config() #> creating sampleName from file_name column #> completing cases #> completing cases done #> setup done lfq <- LFQData$new(bb$data, bb$config) res1 <- summarize_stats(lfq)  res2 <- prolfqua::sim_lfq_data_2factor_config() #> creating sampleName from file_name column #> completing cases #> completing cases done #> setup done res2$config$factor_depth <- 2 lfq2 <- LFQData$new(res2$data, res2$config) stats <- summarize_stats(lfq2) stopifnot(nrow(stats) == 40)  stats <- summarize_stats(lfq2, factor_key = lfq2$factor_keys()[1]) stopifnot(nrow(stats) == 20) stats <- summarize_stats(lfq2, factor_key = lfq2$factor_keys()[2]) stopifnot(nrow(stats) == 20) stats <- summarize_stats(lfq2, factor_key = NULL) stopifnot(nrow(stats) == 10)  bb <- prolfqua::sim_lfq_data_protein_config() #> creating sampleName from file_name column #> completing cases #> completing cases done #> setup done lfq <- LFQData$new(bb$data, bb$config) res1 <- summarize_stats_all(lfq) stopifnot((res1 |> dplyr::filter(group_ == "All") |> nrow()) == (res1 |> nrow())) library(ggplot2) bb1 <- prolfqua::sim_lfq_data_peptide_config() #> creating sampleName from file_name column #> completing cases #> completing cases done #> setup done lfq <- LFQData$new(bb1$data, bb1$config) stats_res <- summarize_stats(lfq) sq <- summarize_stats_quantiles(stats_res, lfq$relevant_factor_keys()) sq <- summarize_stats_quantiles(stats_res, lfq$relevant_factor_keys(), stats = "CV") sq <- summarize_stats_quantiles(stats_res, lfq$relevant_factor_keys(), stats = "sd") xx <- summarize_stats_quantiles(stats_res, lfq$relevant_factor_keys(), probs = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) ggplot2::ggplot(xx$long, aes(x = probs, y = quantiles, color = group_)) + geom_line() + geom_point()

code: set.seed(10) nrPep <- 10000 nrProtein <- 800 p.value <- runif(nrPep) estimate <- rnorm(nrPep) avgAbd <- runif(nrPep) protein_Id <- sample(1:800, size = nrPep,   replace = TRUE, prob = dexp(seq(0,5,length = 800)))  plot(table(table(protein_Id)))   testdata <- data.frame(contrast = "contrast1",   protein_Id = protein_Id,   estimate = estimate,   pseudo_estimate = estimate,   p.value = p.value,   avgAbd = avgAbd )  xx30 <- summary_ROPECA_median_p.scaled(testdata,                                     subject_id = "protein_Id",                                     estimate = "estimate",                                     p.value = "p.value",                                     max.n = 30)  xx2 <- summary_ROPECA_median_p.scaled(testdata,                                     subject_id = "protein_Id",                                     estimate = "estimate",                                     p.value = "p.value",                                     max.n = 1)  testthat::expect_equal(mad(xx2$estimate, na.rm = TRUE),0.384409, tolerance = 1e-4) testthat::expect_equal(median(xx2$estimate), -0.006874857, tolerance = 1e-4) testthat::expect_equal(xx2$beta.based.significance[1],0.819, tolerance = 1e-3) testthat::expect_equal(xx2$beta.based.significance[2],0.9234362,tolerance = 1e-3)  # Uniform distribution hist(testdata$p.value)  hist(xx30$median.p.scaled, breaks = 20)  hist(xx2$median.p.scaled, breaks = 20)  # shows that beta.based.significance has NO uniform distribution # although H0 is true for all cases.  hist(xx30$beta.based.significance, breaks = 20)  hist(xx2$beta.based.significance, breaks = 20)   hist(xx2$median.p.value, breaks = 20)  hist(xx2$beta.based.significance, breaks = 20)  hist(estimate)
